newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr moving narrowly in Tokyo, may test topside.
newsitem.headline: Dlr moving narrowly in Tokyo, may test topside.

text.p: *Dollar moving narrowly in early Tokyo trading near New York session high of 116.78 yen.
*There is talk in market that stop-loss buying by U.S. operators may emerge near 117 yen, a trust bank dealer said.
*He added dollar may test topside if traders begin buying dollars in an attempt to hit these stops.
*But exporters offers and possible long-liquidation sales by securities houses may weigh on dollar, dealers said.
*Dealers said traders are reluctant to buy marks aggressively with sentiment dented by worries about European monetary union and political uncertainty in Europe, keeping mark top-heavy near 69 yen.
*Weakness of German currency against yen may indirectly weigh on dollar/yen rate, they added.
*But the trust bank dealer said: "The dollar has been bought against European currencies. Further short-covering in the dollar against the mark could push up the dollar/yen rate."
*Bids from Japanese investors and possibly from importers expected below 116 yen, supporting greenback.

*Another trust bank dealer said importers who had failed to buy dollars near the 112-113 yen level previously may decide to buy dollars below 116 yen, making the greenback's downside solid. But a city bank dealers said such moves were unlikely.
*Expectations of commercial buying at end of month may push dollar up against yen ahead of Japan's local fixing at 0100 GMT, some dealers said.

*Dealers said they will watch closely for possible comments on Japanese interest rates by Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita at his regular news conference at 0600 GMT, but they added the impact of such comments on currencies may be limited.

*"Japanese interest rates have had an upward bias recently, so even if he (Matsushita) says something on rates, it may not push the dollar down sharply below 115 yen. But we are still paying close attention to his news conference," another city bank dealer said.

*In New York, French National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin, one of the potential successors to outgoing French Prime Minister Alain Juppe, sent dollar to session highs by saying he favours looser fiscal criteria and a larger pool of entrants in the first wave of EMU.
